title: Credit Builder Accounts Closing, Release and Reapplication Terms by Plan
content:
Closing and release figures for the six Credit Builder Accounts plans.

| Plan | Release of savings after the closing date (business days) | Wait after an early closure before a new application (calendar days) | Wait after a delinquency closure before a new application (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Credit Builder 600 Plan | 10 | 30 | 365 |
| Credit Builder 1000 Plan | 10 | 30 | 365 |
| Credit Builder 1200 Plan | 10 | 30 | 365 |
| Credit Builder 1800 Plan | 10 | 30 | 365 |
| Credit Builder 2400 Plan | 7 | 0 | 365 |
| Credit Builder 3000 Plan | 7 | 0 | 365 |

| Term | Every plan |
|---|---|
| Borrower may close before maturity | yes |
| Days a pending early-closure request waits for the borrower's confirmation before it lapses | 14 calendar days |
| Ways released savings can be paid out | ACH to the bank account, or mailed check |
| Fee for releasing savings by mailed check | 0.00 USD |
| Interest owed when savings pay off the loan at an early or delinquency closing | loan balance times the APR divided by 365 times the days from the last due date paid through the closing date, rounded to the cent |

## Meaning of each figure

- **Release:** the business days after the closing date within which released savings are sent.
- **Early-closure wait:** the calendar days after an early closure before a new Credit Builder application is taken; 0 means a new application is taken straight away.
- **Delinquency-closure wait:** the calendar days after a delinquency closure before a new Credit Builder application is taken.
- **Confirmation days:** the calendar days a pending early-closure request waits for the borrower's confirmation before it lapses.
